## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk roadmap-versioned-feedback-revision-chain  # optional interactive review of the saved findings

- HIGH `[active-candidate-review-lineage]` [confidence: limited]: The active-candidate lifecycle does not define what becomes active when the existing review flow creates a distinct sealed replacement: `roadmap_candidate_review.answer_candidate_question` materializes a replacement and `seal_review` binds it, while step 8 (`Bind candidate questions, answers, rejection, and discard resolution to the exact active-candidate batch`), step 9 (`Promote only the exact active candidate for the current root`), and the acceptance criteria allow processing only for the root/active pair. Leaving the initial candidate active makes its sealed replacement unpromotable; replacing it changes proposal-currentness and provenance without a stated transition. Architecture says:

```text
“Processing reads only this pair: the accepted root and the active candidate, when present.”
```

Acceptance criteria says:

```text
“Processing considers only the explicit accepted-root and active-candidate pair; candidates outside that pair remain preserved history and are ignored.”
```
  - Plan-altitude restatement (delivered evidence, not a verdict on this finding): Define how a review-produced replacement enters, replaces, or remains outside the active-candidate lifecycle so review and promotion address the same exact candidate.
  - Fix: Specify the active-pointer and proposal-provenance transition for review replacements, then reconcile steps 5, 8, 9, and the lifecycle acceptance criteria to that rule.
- HIGH `[candidate-rejection-discard-boundary]` [confidence: limited]: Step 8 requires review rejection and an explicit discard command to resolve and release an active candidate, but `## Out of scope` excludes “a new approve/edit/reject protocol” and changes to individual candidate operations beyond consuming a batch snapshot. The current `roadmap_candidate_review` lifecycle provides question, answer, replacement, and seal operations, not rejection or discard; the plan never resolves whether these are authorized extensions of that lifecycle or deliberately excluded work. Architecture says:

```text
“A review rejection automatically records a terminal rejected resolution, releases the active-candidate pointer, and preserves that candidate and its proposals as historical stale evidence. An operator may invoke the same candidate-lifecycle owner through an explicit discard command…”
```

`## Out of scope` says:

```text
“Changing stage operation authority, roadmap gates, or individual candidate operations except to consume a batch snapshot rather than embedded feedback.”
```
  - Fix: Define the allowed candidate-lifecycle boundary for rejection and discard, including whether the existing review protocol gains those operations, and align step 8 and the out-of-scope contract.
- MEDIUM `[accepted-head-writers]` [confidence: limited]: The accepted-head writer set conflicts: `## Overview` calls exact review-seal promotion the only advancing operation, while `## Architecture`, `## Scope guardrails`, and the acceptance criteria also make enrolled decision settlement an accepted-head writer. This leaves the settlement handshake either unsupported by the top-level architecture or an exception to its stated exclusivity. `## Overview` says:

```text
“Exact review-seal promotion remains the only operation that advances the accepted artifact head…”
```

`## Architecture` says:

```text
“Guarded root enrollment creates the initial accepted head; exact review-seal promotion and the existing enrolled decision-settlement path are the only subsequent accepted-head writers.”
```
  - Fix: State one consistent accepted-head writer set across the overview, architecture, scope guardrails, and acceptance criteria.

## Suggested next steps

- Close 3 conceptual-correctness gap(s) through a session-directed edit now (design gaps; not auto-applied under #85); completeness gaps stay informational until a complete detail bundle exists.
